canonicalExplanation.summary: Every object has a **lifetime**: the time its storage exists. **Automatic** objects (locals) live until their block `{ }` ends. **Static** objects live for the whole program. **Allocated** objects (from malloc) live until `free`. A pointer **doesn't keep anything alive**: when the object's lifetime ends, every pointer to it becomes **dangling**, even though the address bits look unchanged. So think in terms of **ownership**. The **owner** is responsible for releasing the resource; **borrowers** may use it only while the owner keeps it alive. Write down who owns what and **where it's released**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner keeps a pointer to a buffer declared inside an `if` block so they can use it later. Printing through it works in a debug build and shows garbage in an optimised one. A pointer to a block automatic array becomes dangling when execution leaves that block even if the address bits remain unchanged. In this lesson you'll identify owner, borrowers and release point for each resource in a routine.

examples.title: The array that left its block
examples.situation: A pointer to a block automatic array becomes dangling when execution leaves that block even if the address bits remain unchanged.
walkthrough: **A pointer to a block automatic array:** saved = buf inside the if block.
**Becomes dangling when execution leaves that block:** buf's lifetime ends at the closing brace.
**Even if the address bits remain unchanged:** saved still prints the same address, but reading through it will be undefined; point at static keep or copy the text instead.
examples.result: The label prints reliably in every build.

examples.title: The config pointer
examples.situation: load_config() reads a file into a local char array and returns a struct holding a pointer into that array.
walkthrough: The array dies when load_config returns, so the struct holds dangling pointers.
Owner options: store the text inside the struct (char name[64]) or allocate it and make the caller the owner.
examples.result: Every field of the config stays valid as long as the config itself.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Keeping a pointer variable alive keeps its pointed-to object alive as well.
misconceptions.correction: Pointers don't affect lifetime. When the object's block ends, or it's freed, every pointer to it becomes dangling.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what ended buf's lifetime?

analogy.example: Lifetime is like **a library book loan**. The library (owner) decides when the book is returned. Your note of its shelf number (pointer) doesn't keep the book on the shelf: after it's returned, the shelf may hold something else. Borrowers read only during the loan.
usefulFor: remembering the note doesn't keep the book
limitations: Libraries tell you the due date; C doesn't.
Static storage is a book the library never lends out.

artifact: if block: char buf[16]; saved = buf;

steps.explanation: A pointer to a block automatic array is stored while buf is alive.
The pointer becomes dangling when execution leaves that block.
Pointing at an object that lives long enough makes later use valid.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a dangling pointer. Step 1, Borrow: buf is alive; saved is &buf[0]. A pointer to a block automatic array is stored while buf is alive. Step 2, End: buf is lifetime over; saved is same address bits. The pointer becomes dangling when execution leaves that block. Step 3, Fix: saved is &keep[0] (static). Pointing at an object that lives long enough makes later use valid.

nearTransfer.prompt: For a given function with a local array, a static counter and a malloc'd buffer, write a table: owner, borrowers, lifetime end, release point. Mark any pointer used after its object's lifetime.
scaffold: Look for addresses stored beyond their block.

farTransfer.prompt: Rewrite load_config so every pointer it returns is valid until free_config is called. Document ownership in the header, and test with -fsanitize=address, including a deliberate use-after-free to see the report.

expectedEvidence: Sanitizer clean except the deliberate test.

remediation.explanation: For every pointer write: **who owns the object, when does its lifetime end, and is every use before that point?**

recap.summary: To identify owners, borrowers and release points, remember automatic objects end with their block, static ones with the program and allocated ones at free, pointers never extend lifetime and become dangling when their object ends, and each resource needs one clear owner who releases it.
